observation.visible_scene: Over-the-shoulder / helmet-cam view of a paddler in turbulent whitewater rapids. The foreground figure wears a green-and-black helmet with a small action camera mounted on top and a yellow flotation vest; only the back of their head and shoulders are visible. Midstream, a person in a bright green top and yellow helmet stands on a rock in the churning water, facing the foreground paddler. Further back, a person in yellow stands atop a large grey boulder. On the right bank, a crowd of spectators sits and stands on rocks watching. The background is an autumn forest of bare trunks and brown/orange foliage, with a pale overcast sky. White water fills the channel between large boulders on the left and right.
visible_changes: The whitewater churns and boils continuously throughout the segment, with foam and splashes reshaping every frame.

The viewpoint drifts slowly downstream/forward: relative to the frame edges the foreground helmet stays roughly centered but the left boulder, foreground leaves, and the midstream green-shirted person shift slightly in position and scale, indicating the camera platform (the paddler) is moving rather than the scene rearranging.

A faint greyish spray/mist patch above the central boulder becomes more defined and visible within the first few frames (around t=0.2–0.4s) and then persists as a standing plume of water spray for the rest of the clip.
The yellow-clad figure on the boulder makes small postural movements but remains in place; the green-shirted midstream person stays standing on the same rock, occasionally shifting their arms.
Spectators on the right bank remain seated/standing with minor posture changes; a few raise their arms/hands at points, but no one leaves or enters the bank area.
No discrete action begins or ends inside the crop; the paddling-through-rapids state is already ongoing at frame 1 and continues past the last frame.
outside_clip_unknowns: What produces the background spray plume (e.g., an upstream drop, a slide, or another paddler) is not shown.
The purpose or prior/next motion of the yellow figure on the boulder and of the green-shirted midstream person is unknown.
Whether the foreground paddler ultimately drops into a rapid feature or stops is outside the segment.
The exact mounting of the camera (helmet vs. handheld) cannot be confirmed from these frames alone.
uncertain_details: The slow perspective drift could be partly camera bobbing on the moving paddler rather than net downstream translation; magnitude is small.
The source and nature of the mist/spray patch are inferred only from its appearance, not from a visible cause.
Minor arm/posture changes of distant figures are hard to track precisely at this resolution.
